newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares register sharp fall in bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares register sharp fall in bourse trade.

text.p: German shares end bourse trade sharply lower on Tuesday, as dealers said market nervousness at recent record levels on the DAX index was finally translating into a long-anticipated correction.
The DAX-30 index ended down 53.97 points, or 1.78 percent, at 2,976.71 points in early bourse trade and the March DAX future contract was down 17 points at 2,997 points.

"We started off brightly but no-one really knew why. There is a lot of nervousness about and there has been for a while, and you wouldn't want to get carried away with optimism on a day like this," said one trader.
A strong performer in both pre-bourse trade and early bourse trade was the banking sector, particularly Germany's biggest bank Deutsche Bank AG and Commerzbank AG.
However, the banks followed the market downwards over the session. Deutsche ended the day down 74 pfennigs at 80.50 marks and Commerzbank ended the day down 55 pfennigs at 44.10 marks.

Shares in chemicals and metals group Degussa AG ended up 15 marks at 730 marks -- totally against the general run of play in the markets -- after the group said pre-tax profits jumped 20 percent in the first quarter of the 1996/97 business year.

Another big gainer was the drugs and chemicals group Merck KGaA, which was up 2.10 marks at 60.35 marks after reporting an 11.3 percent rise in 1996 group sales and forecasting a strong profit growth for the year.
Airline Lufthansa shares also ended the day higher, up 44 pfennigs at 22.80 marks, as dealers said the stock broke through a point of technical resistance.

Such resistance points occur for financial securities because of the balance of demand and supply in the market. Once a security has breached a resistance point, it can often go on to make large gains.
German equities took a hit after the west German business climate index from the research institute Ifo fell to 95.8 in December from 96.9.
However, dealers said that there had been rumours of a fall to 95.5 and attributed the decline more to overall market jitters than anything specifically related to the Ifo figures.
